ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
1.

Pursuant to the order dated 17.10.2023 passed by us, the affidavit of the Collector, Ahmedabad - respondent No.1 herein has been placed before us to demonstrate that the lands in Survey Nos.616 Maheshkumar Ambalal Patel vs The Competent Authority And Additional ... on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19106114/
1 and 621 (old Block No.1224) situated at Village Visalpur, Taluka Daskroi, District Ahmedabad
were not subject matter of acquisition in the notifications issued under Section 3(A) and 3(D) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined 2.

It is stated that the controversy in the present petition has arisen on account of identification and location of the lands in question pursuant to resurvey and promulgation of land records by the State Government in the year 2016.

It is stated that after completion of the promulgation of record proceedings and consolidation of Survey Nos.616 and 621, and Survey Nos.623 and 624 in the year 2016, the village map of lands bearing Survey Nos.623 and 624 (old Block No.1223/2/b) were erroneously reflected the said plots in place of Survey Nos.616 and 621 (old Block No.1224), which was prepared pursuant to resurvey and promulgation of land records in the year 2016.

At the time of acquisition for the purpose of construction of National Highway No.751, Ahmedabad - Dholera Express Way, the village map of Visalpur of the year 2016 was considered by the competent authority for identification of the lands required for acquisition purposes.

entities.text: National Highway No.751, Ahmedabad - Dholera Express Way
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The alignment of National Highway though passes through Survey Nos.616 and NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined 621 (old Block No.1224), but the same was erroneously identified as passing through Survey Nos.623 and 624, shown in the village map since the year 2016.

3. It is stated in paragraph '3.3 and 3.4' of the affidavit of the Collector that the office of the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) had intimated the office of DILR (District Inspector of Land Records), Ahmedabad to conduct a resurvey of the lands in question and pass a fresh order.

On the said intimation, vide communication dated 07.06.2023, the respondent No.1 has decided to grant compensation to the land owners of Survey Nos.616 and 621 (old Block No.1224) as per the proposal that had been sent after such lands had been resurveyed.

It is, thus, contended that the communication dated 08.06.2023 issued by the office of the Collector intimating the petitioners to receive compensation had been issued pursuant to the rectification measurement order dated 25.05.2023 passed by the DILR, Ahmedabad, which in NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined turn had been issued consequent to the communication sent by the NHAI.

4. Taking note of the above contentions in the affidavit of the Collector, it is more than evident that the lands belonging to the petitioners namely Survey Nos.616 and 621 was not subject matter of acquisition proceedings as it was not included in the acquisition notifications published under Section 3(A) and 3(D) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
The awards with respect to the acquisition in question were passed on 29.06.2019 and 07.09.2021 wherein the lands in Survey Nos.623 and 624 were indicated as the acquired lands.

It seems that the amended awards were passed, as admittedly after correction of the village map on the communication sent by the NHAI after having an inquiry into the mistake which had occurred at the time of preparation of village map after completion of the promulgation proceedings in the year 2016.

sentences.text: In our considered opinion, the lands in question namely Survey Nos.616 and 621 which were NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined not part of the acquisition proceedings could not have been included by making amendment in the awards dated 29.06.2019 and 07.09.2021.
The reason being that the award pertains to determination of compensation of the acquired land only.

The land which is not subject matter of acquisition cannot be made part of the award by making an amendment substituting the plots in question with other two plots which were part of the acquisition notifications.
The said approach of the office of the Collector in making amendment in the award by passing amended awards on 08.06.2023 is found to be erroneous.

6. We may note that the National Highways Act, 1956 provides right of objections to the person interested on issuance of notification under Section 3(A) wherein proposal for acquisition of any land is published.

Section 3(C) of the Act, 1956 provides for hearing of objections of any person interested in the land within thirty one days from the date of publication of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined notification.

The declaration notification under Section 3(D) is issued only after disposal of the objections of the persons interested which results in vesting of the land subject matter of acquisition with the Central Government.
The question of taking possession of the acquired lands comes only after the vesting takes place under Section 3(D).

Section 3(F) further provides that where the land has vested with the Central Government under Section 3(D), it shall be lawful for any person authorized by the Central Government in that behalf to enter and do other acts necessary upon the land for carrying out the building, maintenance, management or operation of a national highway or part thereof, or any other work connected therewith.

The power to enter into the acquired land vested in the Central Government under Section 3(F) is subject to the provisions of Section 3(E) which provides that the notice in writing directing the owners or any other person to surrender or deliver possession of the land vested NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined with the Central Government shall be issued only upon determination of the compensation by the competent authority under Section 3(G) and deposit of the same in accordance with the provisions of Section 3(H)(1) of the Act, 1956.
7. In the instant case, as noted hereinabove, the lands in question were not subject matter of acquisition proceedings.

The petitioners have rushed to this Court by filing the instant writ petition on 06.07.2023, challenging the amended awards dated 08.06.2023 and the consequent acquisition of their plots bearing Survey Nos.616 and 621, by inclusion of the said lands in the award passed on 29.06.2019.
At that stage, at the time of admission of the writ petition on 13.07.2023, this Court has passed an order directing the parties to maintain status-quo with respect to the lands in question.

By order dated 17.10.2023, we have opined that on account of any error in the revenue entries, which was corrected later by the revenue authorities, the alignment of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined National Highways cannot be changed or the construction of the national highway which is about 300 meters of stretch cannot be put to halt.

Saying so we have vacated the interim order dated 13.07.2023 permitting the National Highway Authority to carry out the construction work on the spot and further directed the petitioners not to raise any obstruction in the work to be carried out by the National Highway Authority on the spot taking note of the fact that the said work is essentially of public nature.

However, at the same time we have opined that the for the utilization of the lands in question, the petitioners would be entitled to claim compensation.

8. The question which has come up today is as to what would be the date of determination of the compensation in the case of the petitioners whose lands in Survey Nos.616 and 621 have been utilized though they were not included in the acquisition proceedings.

Taking note of the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956, we find that though NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined there was a determination of compensation by awards dated 29.06.2019 and 07.09.2021 but the said determination cannot be said to be determination of compensation for the lands in question namely Survey Nos.616 and 621.

The deposit of compensation by the National Highway Authority under the aforesaid award for lands in Survey Nos.623 and 624 cannot be treated as the deposit of compensation for the lands belonging to the petitioners which came into picture with the passing of the amended awards both dated 08.06.2023.
Indisputably, the fact remains that the petitioners have not been granted any right of hearing during the entire proceedings of amended awards dated 08.06.2023.
It is, thus, not permitted for the respondents to assert that they were entitled to take possession of the lands in question namely Survey Nos.616 and 621 by passing amended awards dated 08.06.2023.

The petitioners having rushed to this Court challenging the amended awards have invited attention of the Court to the error committed on the part of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED:
12/02/2024 undefined office of the Collector and the amended awards dated 08.06.2023 have been found to be the awards without acquisition of the lands in Survey Nos.616 and 621, which would have required publication of the declaration notifications under Section 3(A), giving opportunity of objection to the petitioners under Section 3(C) and then publication of declaration notifications under Section 3(D).
9.

As the process of acquisition has not been undertaken and the petitioners have agitated their claim before this Court by filing the instant petition wherein possession of the lands in question has been taken under the order dated 17.10.2023 passed by us, in our considered opinion, the interest of justice would be met if the date of determination of the compensation with respect to the lands in question namely Survey Nos.616 and 621 is determined by considering the market value as the date of institution of the instant writ petition, which is 06.07.2023.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined 10.

We, therefore, direct the Collector to initiate fresh proceedings for determination of compensation for the lands in question namely Survey Nos.616 and 621 by treating the date of institution of the writ petition, i.e. 06.07.2023 as the date of acquisition, i.e. issuance of preliminary notification under Section 3(A) of the National Highways Act, 1956 to compute the market value of the lands in question as on the said date.

Other elements of compensation as admissible to be paid under the National Highways Act, 1956 or any other applicable laws, shall be duly computed and made part of the award to be prepared by the Special Land Acquisition Officer under the directions issued by the Collector.
In the proceedings for preparation of the award, the petitioners herein as also the National Highway Authority shall be entitled to participate.

Due notice shall be given to both the parties calling upon them to participate in the proceedings of preparation of the award,

4 wherein they are obliged NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11898/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined to cooperate.

sentences.text: The determination by the Competent Authority shall be made strictly in accordance with the provisions of Section 3(G) of the National Highways Act, 1956 and other applicable laws for making an award, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of four months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
It is further clarified that the parties to the award shall be free to agitate their right by availing further remedy as available under the National Highways Act, 1956.
11. The instant petition is disposed of, accordingly.
